title: In a high-income small island economy, aging, skills shortages, high costs, and digital access determine whether growth becomes good work and intergenerational mobility
source_unit: World Bank Group, 2026 Seychelles Country Growth and Jobs Report: Modernize, Utilize, Digitalize: How to Raise Productivity to Deliver Growth, Good Jobs, and Social Mobility, summarized September 17, 2026
geography: Seychelles, a small island economy with high income per capita, geographic isolation, aging pressures, and a narrow labor market

observations.period: September 2026; growth capacity and small-island constraints

growth_record.value: the report describes Seychelles as having achieved more than three decades of economic growth and one of Africa’s highest income-per-capita levels

constraints.value: aging, skills shortages, small size, and geographic isolation are identified as pressures on sustaining economic performance

translation_question.value: the policy question is whether productivity and private-sector reform can create quality jobs and social mobility rather than only preserve aggregate income

observations.method: World Bank country growth-and-jobs report summarized in an official press release.
observations.uncertainty: The press release does not provide the report’s full sectoral, distributional, demographic, or labor-market estimates, and does not establish causal effects of the proposed reforms.
observations.subgroup: Young people, older workers, firms, workers facing skills shortages, households, and future generations in a small and geographically isolated economy.
observations.counterinterpretation: Small size and isolation can constrain scale, but can also enable coordinated reforms if institutions, employers, and education systems align.

observations.period: 2040; modeled reform scenario and household purchasing power

denominator.unit: World Bank accelerated-reform scenario for Seychelles

gdp.unit: percent potential GDP increase by 2040 under proposed reforms

jobs.unit: additional jobs projected under the scenario

better_paid_jobs.unit: equivalent better-paying jobs projected under the scenario

real_wages.unit: percent potential increase in real wages

purchasing_power.unit: percent potential increase in household purchasing power

observations.method: World Bank scenario estimates reported in the official country-report release.
observations.uncertainty: These are modeled potential gains, not observed outcomes; they do not establish who receives jobs, wage gains, or purchasing-power improvements, or how costs are distributed.
observations.subgroup: Workers, households, young people, firms, and future generations affected by productivity and labor-market reforms.
observations.counterinterpretation: Aggregate wage and purchasing-power gains can mask unequal access, migration effects, housing costs, or job displacement in a small labor market.

observations.period: September 2026; labor-market modernization and youth transition

denominator.unit: World Bank Modernize and Utilize reform framework

modernize.value: the report calls for updating labor regulations, reforming foreign-labor management, reducing barriers to trade and investment, and strengthening commercial justice

human_capital.value: the report calls for addressing youth vulnerability, improving education and workforce skills, and strengthening school-to-work pathways

mobility_route.value: the central open route is whether education and workforce systems produce usable skills, job access, earnings, and intergenerational mobility

observations.method: World Bank report priorities summarized in the official release.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not report youth employment, school-to-work transition, vacancy, migration, wage, or skill-mismatch microdata, nor evaluate the proposed reforms.
observations.subgroup: Young people, students, foreign and domestic workers, employers, educators, and households planning across generations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Labor-market modernization can improve matching and productivity, but reforming foreign labor and regulation may also redistribute opportunity or weaken protections if worker voice is not preserved.

observations.period: September 2026; digitalization, affordability, and public-service access

digital_transformation.value: digital transformation is presented as a productivity, innovation, entrepreneurship, and public-service-delivery priority

access_conditions.value: the proposed route includes improving internet quality and affordability, expanding digital government services, and strengthening digital skills

dependency_test.value: digitalization becomes inclusive only if people can afford access, use services, retain alternatives, and contest errors or exclusion

observations.method: World Bank country-report strategy and reform priorities summarized in the official release.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not report current connectivity, affordability, digital-skill gaps, public-service uptake, privacy safeguards, or distributional effects.
observations.subgroup: Young people, older residents, rural or remote users, low-income households, entrepreneurs, public-service users, and workers exposed to digital transition.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital government can reduce distance and administrative friction, but it can also shift costs and responsibilities onto users when connectivity, support, and appeal routes are weak.

related_sources.claim: Zimbabwe Growth and Jobs provides a contrasting route where growth and stabilization coexist with mass informality and weak household translation.
Brazil Paraíba water-security work provides complementary infrastructure and service-access context.

boundary: This record adds a small-island growth-to-household route from aging, skills shortages, isolation, labor-market and business reform, human capital, digital access, and public services through projected jobs, wages, purchasing power, and social mobility. It is a country-report summary with modeled scenarios, not a causal evaluation, household panel, or proof of equitable gains.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official World Bank September 17, 2026 press release was reviewed for Seychelles growth context, aging and isolation pressures, modeled GDP/jobs/wage/purchasing-power gains, labor-market modernization, youth skills, school-to-work pathways, digital adoption, internet affordability, digital government, and skills priorities.
